resumen: The bar sits in front, on the shoulders. The torso stays more upright than in the back squat and the knee takes less compression.
ejecucion: Rack the bar on your front delts, in front of your neck, and cross your arms over it: each hand on the opposite shoulder.
Feet shoulder-width apart, turned slightly out.
Lower by bending hips and knees, keeping the torso as upright as you can.
Go at least to thighs parallel to the floor, if your mobility allows.
Drive up through the whole foot, without letting the elbows drop.
matices: The comparison with the back squat is measured: the back squat produced 11.0 N/kg of knee compressive force against 9.3 N/kg for the front squat, with similar muscle activation. That is why the front squat is often proposed when the knee is a problem. The trade-off is that it asks more of your ankles. It is shown here with crossed arms; the clean grip, hands on the bar, asks a lot of the wrists and is the other usual option.

fuentes.titulo: A Biomechanical Comparison of Back and Front Squats in Healthy Trained Individuals
